Querulous

KWEHR-yuh-luss · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Querulous is habitually complaining in a whining, peevish manner.

By the third hour of the delayed flight, the passenger's querulous complaints about every minor inconvenience had worn out the gate agent's patience.

Worked Example

Nothing satisfied the querulous customer, who found something new to complain about at every stage of the meal.

Finding something new to complain about at every stage of a meal, no matter what, is exactly querulous.

How Querulous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

whiny

whiny: complaining in a childish or irritating way

peevish

peevish: easily irritated and inclined to complain

Antonyms

uncomplaining

uncomplaining: not inclined to express dissatisfaction

How Strong Is It? — fussy → querulous → cantankerous

fussy vs. querulous

fussy vs. querulous: Fussy suggests mild, occasional pickiness -- a light, everyday word; querulous describes a nonstop, wearing pattern of complaint.

cantankerous vs. querulous

cantankerous vs. querulous: Cantankerous (taught earlier in this course) adds outright quarrelsomeness and prickly irritability, while querulous is more specifically about the whining TONE of the complaints themselves.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — quer

root — quer: to complain (Latin (queri))

suffix — -ulous

suffix — -ulous: tending to, full of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Querulous comes from Latin queri ('to complain') + -ulous ('tending to') -- literally 'tending to complain.'

Use the root in a new word: quarrel

Use the root in a new word: quarrel: The same queri root, by way of Latin querela, gives us the everyday word quarrel -- an argument that often grows out of exactly this kind of complaining.
